terms.gloss: at the house of, with (a person)
evidence: Catull. 13.1: cēnābis bene, mī Fabulle, apud mē
Plaut. Aul. 243: hīc apud mē hortum cōnfodere jussī
terms.comment: With a person, at their home: apud mē, at my house; apud avum, at Grandpa’s. Also in someone’s presence (apud jūdicem), and among a people (see among).

evidence: Cic. Att. 4.4a.1: perbellē fēceris sī ad nōs vēneris
terms.comment: With verbs of motion: ad mē venī, come to my house; ad avum īmus, we are going to Grandpa’s.

evidence: Cic. Att. 1.12.3: dēprehēnsum domī C. Caesaris
terms.comment: Domī meae, at my house; domī Caesaris, at Caesar’s house. Going there, domum meam.

phrases.latin: cēnābis bene, mī Fabulle, apud mē paucīs, sī tibi dī favent, diēbus
phrases.english: you will dine well at my house, my Fabullus, in a few days, if the gods are kind to you

phrases.latin: Hīc apud mē hortum cōnfodere jussī.
phrases.english: I’ve had the garden dug over here at my place.

phrases.latin: perbellē fēceris sī ad nōs vēneris
phrases.english: it would be lovely of you to come to us

phrases.latin: P. Clōdium Appī f., crēdō tē audīsse cum veste muliebrī dēprehēnsum domī C. Caesaris
phrases.english: I expect you have heard that Publius Clodius, son of Appius, was caught in women’s clothes at Gaius Caesar’s house
Today we’re having dinner at Grandpa’s.
